input: Get a notarized letter for my landlord dispute

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The specific purpose of the letter (e.g., disputing a security deposit, uninhabitable conditions, illegal entry, lease violation) completely changes what content needs to be written and what claims must be substantiated.
Knowing who is writing and signing the letter (the tenant themselves, a witness, a co-tenant, an attorney) determines whose identity needs notarizing and what authority the letter carries.
The stage of the dispute (pre-negotiation, formal demand, court filing, response to landlord) affects the urgency, tone, and legal weight required of the letter.
The deadline by which the notarized letter must be delivered dictates how quickly the user must act and which notarization options (in-person, online/remote) are viable.
Whether the user already has a draft of the letter or needs to write one from scratch determines the immediate first action — drafting vs. finding a notary.
The user's preferred notarization method (bank, UPS/shipping store, online remote notary, mobile notary) affects cost, convenience, and turnaround time.

Knowing what the letter needs to achieve (pressure the landlord to act, satisfy a legal filing requirement, serve as evidence) defines what 'done well' looks like and whether legal review is necessary.

gold.taskTitle: Get a notarized letter for landlord dispute
gold.taskDescription: The user needs to obtain a notarized letter to support or resolve a dispute with their landlord.

questions.title: What specific issue is this dispute about?
questions.description: Identify the core subject of the dispute — e.g., withheld security deposit, mold/habitability, illegal entry, eviction, lease violations — so the letter addresses the right claims.

questions.title: Who will be signing the notarized letter?
questions.description: Clarify whether the signer is the tenant, a witness, a co-tenant, or an attorney, as this determines whose identity the notary must verify and the letter's legal standing.

questions.title: What stage is the dispute at right now?
questions.description: Determine whether this is an early warning letter, a formal demand, a response to the landlord, or a document being submitted to a court or housing authority.

questions.title: When does this letter need to be delivered?
questions.description: Establish the hard deadline for delivery so the plan accounts for drafting time, notary appointment availability, and any legal notice windows.

questions.title: Do you already have a written draft of the letter?
questions.description: Find out if the user needs help writing the letter from scratch or if they already have text ready and only need notarization.

questions.title: How do you prefer to get the letter notarized?
questions.description: Identify the user's preferred method — visiting a bank/UPS store, using an online remote notary service, or hiring a mobile notary — to match convenience and timing.

questions.title: What outcome does this letter need to achieve?
questions.description: Clarify whether the goal is to pressure the landlord to comply, satisfy a legal filing requirement, document a claim as evidence, or something else, so the tone and content can be calibrated.
